prompt: Let $A$ be a set and $R\subseteq A\times A$ a binary relation on $A$. For $x,y\in A$, write $R(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in R$. Which property is defined exactly by $\forall x\in A\; R(x,x)$?

answers.explanation: Every element has a self-loop; pairs of different elements are unrestricted.
No element has a self-loop; pairs of different elements are unrestricted. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Every related pair has its reverse; loops are allowed but not required. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Every two-step chain has its direct shortcut, including chains with repeated vertices. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Only one element needs to relate to itself. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Each element has at least one outgoing related element, which may be itself. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
All diagonal pairs and no off-diagonal pairs are present. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Every pair is comparable, including an element with itself, so all loops are required. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Every ordered pair is present, including every loop. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Every related pair is diagonal; some or all loops may be missing. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
